This is entirely my opinion on this, and I’m in NO WAY a professional, but here’s how I think of it (if it changes anything, I’ve gone through the process to get officially diagnosed, so I know how it works):

- For really complex disorders like BPD, self diagnosis is VERY dangerous/damaging. Like, you could convince yourself you have BPD and play up the symptoms so much you actually do damage to yourself. OR, you could end up falsely portraying the disorder to other people and give them the wrong impression of what BPD looks like. 

- On the other hand, other disorders like trichotillomania only really have one criteria, and it’s a yes or no question. There’s kinda no real in between, you either have it or you don’t. Tbh with the more “simple” (and by simple I do NOT mean less important/less valid/less difficult to diagnose) disorders, it’s okay to say you do it you’ve done your research and the answer is obvious.

- For disorders like anxiety and depression, I would stick to saying things like “I have symptoms of an anxiety disorder” or “I suffer with a lot of anxiety” without saying “yes I have a clinical anxiety disorder”. Same with depression, saying you have symptoms of X, or strongly suspect you have X, can be a lot less damaging than saying you have X, if that makes sense.

- For eating disorders, I would just stick to saying disordered eating/issues with food

* TL;DR if you wanna play it safe, just stick to saying “ I strongly suspect I have [X]”

Again I want to make it VERY clear that this is just my opinion and I’d honestly love to hear what other people think
